sources.title: NGSS 5-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment
U.S. EPA: Recycling Basics and Benefits

steps.title: Recycling bin
steps.instruction: Trace the recycling bin and its lid.

note.text: The loop starts at home or school: cans, bottles and paper go into the recycling bin, not the trash.

steps.title: Truck
steps.instruction: Trace the collection truck and its wheels.

note.text: Trucks collect the recycling. At a facility, it's sorted and cleaned.
The sorted materials are made into new products at a recycling plant.
People buy products made from recycled material. That closes the loop.

steps.title: The loop
steps.instruction: Draw the four arrows around the loop.

note.text: Materials go round and round instead of ending up in a landfill.

steps.title: Around the loop
items: Put the bottle in the recycling bin
A plant makes a new product
steps.why: Recycling is a loop: collect and sort, make new products, then buy them, so the materials get used again.
steps.hint: Where does the bottle go first?

steps.title: Why recycle?
steps.question: How does a community recycling program help protect Earth?

options.text: It saves natural resources and keeps waste out of landfills
options.feedback: Yes. Reusing materials means less digging, cutting and drilling for new ones, and less waste to bury or burn.
Recycling turns used things into new products, so there's less trash.

options.text: It uses up more trees and metal
options.feedback: It's the opposite: recycled material replaces new trees and metal.
It does: it conserves resources and energy, and keeps waste out of landfills.

steps.title: Even better
steps.question: Which is even better for Earth than recycling a plastic bottle?

options.text: Using a refillable bottle so there's less waste to begin with
options.feedback: Right. Reducing and reusing come first. Things should be recycled when they can't be reduced or reused.
Trash goes to a landfill. Reusing a bottle is better, and recycling is better than trash.
That makes more waste. Reusing a refillable bottle makes less.
That's still waste. Reusing a bottle means less waste to begin with.
